clue.text: Where you may end up in stitches in more ways than one

definitions.text: Where you may end up in stitches in more ways than one

parts.words: Where you may end up in stitches in more ways than one
parts.note: an operating venue leaves you with sutures, while a comedy venue leaves you helpless with laughter

explanation.surface: A warning that some outing will leave you either laughing hard or sewn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In stitches' has two senses: laughing uncontrollably at a comedy, or having a wound sewn after surgery. Both happen in the same kind of place: a stage venue and a hospital operating room.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a playhouse and a surgical operating room share this name, covering both senses of stitches.

parts.note: frank means candid, open and honest
someone who consumed food ate it

explanation.surface: A rival in some contest was honest about being a big spender.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is someone standing for selection or election, a synonym in the political sense.

definitions.meaning: coins or small cash handed back after paying
alteration or reform, which people commonly push back against

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that people tend to refuse cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers loose coins and also any alteration, the kind of novelty people habitually oppose.

parts.note: down is the soft fine plumage of birds
cast means thrown, as a line or a stone

explanation.surface: Blue plumes tossed through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour for the feathers, but it is the definition in its sense of sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means low in spirits, a synonym for dejected and gloomy.

clue.text: Big boss arranged credit or information on real diversifying

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of credit or are put into a new order

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: diversifying says the letters of real are varied into another order

explanation.surface: A chief executive who reorganised lending details on property.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is informal British for information. The title is best known as that of the head of the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a large organisation such as the BBC carries this title, so it names the top boss.

clue.text: Beckon over group that's used in radio transmission

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: to beckon someone is to wave them towards you
a band is a group of musicians or people

explanation.surface: Waving a band across, as if summoning musicians to a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beckon over' reads as one phrase meaning summon, but 'over' is only a positional signal in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A range of frequencies allotted for broadcasting is the thing a radio set tunes within.

definitions.meaning: to hamper or confine, as in limiting someone's style
a sudden painful contraction of a muscle

explanation.surface: A sore muscle that limits your movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to hinder or confine, and the noun is a painful involuntary muscle spasm.

clue.text: Partner's issue, being on flight first

indicators.note: first says the flight piece comes ahead of on

parts.note: a flight of stairs is a set of steps

explanation.surface: A spouse's child standing on a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' here means offspring, so a partner's issue is a child of one's spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy from a spouse's earlier relationship is offspring of one's partner but not oneself.

indicators.note: interminable means without an end, so the last letter of the word the goes

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: Fighting off the endless pimples.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat soundly, whether in a fight or a game, is a synonym for trounce.

indicators.note: in says the meat goes inside the rush

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like marsh plant
veal is meat from a calf

explanation.surface: A dish exposed as calf meat cooked in rushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' looks like a verb of haste, but it is the waterside plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncovered has been exposed or disclosed, a synonym for brought to light.

parts.note: a dance done by warriors, put as if it were a ballroom step

explanation.surface: A quip that soldiers have their own ballroom routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The two-step is a ballroom dance; the question mark admits that a ritual dance before battle is a playful stretch of that.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial dance performed before battle, as by some tribes, is a martial form of dancing.

parts.note: by means of, as in travel by train
a pass is a permit to enter

explanation.surface: Getting around a barrier with an official permit.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something by circling past it is a synonym for circumvent.

indicators.note: awkwardly says the letters of treading are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Stepping clumsily on finding oneself on a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope or incline, such as a hill on a road, is measured as a rise over distance.

clue.text: Nothing in temporary accommodation where maiden's sheltered that's soothing

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: sheltered says the maiden is housed inside the temporary accommodation

parts.note: a tent is shelter put up for a short stay
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A camp scene where a young woman finds comfort under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm or salve rubbed on skin to relieve it is the kind of thing that soothes.

parts.note: the mean is the arithmetic average
a swell is an old word for a smartly dressed toff, a posh British gent

explanation.surface: An ordinary upper-class gent who is well-meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for an upper-class person; swell is a dated term for the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone whose aims are kind, even if their actions misfire.

definitions.meaning: round, shaped like a ball or disc
a leaflet or handbill sent out widely

explanation.surface: A pilot or traveller who goes all around the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests an aviator, but it is a printed leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means round in shape and also a mass-distributed leaflet.

definitions.meaning: wide-ranging and all-embracing, as in wholesale changes
the action of using a broom on a floor

explanation.surface: A thorough appraisal of a painter's technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brushwork' suggests painting, but here it is cleaning with a broom.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means far-reaching, and the noun is the act of clearing with a broom.

parts.note: wins means gains or obtains
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A fellow who is putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, as borne by Churchill, stands for any man.

clue.text: Drama, son becoming one of the glamorous idle rich?

definitions.text: one of the glamorous idle rich?

parts.note: a play is a stage drama
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A theatrical lad growing into a wealthy loafer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy man who lives for pleasure and parties typifies the leisured jet set.

indicators.note: wriggling says the letters of ten squirm into a new order

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Landing ten squirming fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' looks like a noun in the surface, but it is the verb meaning to use a rod and line.
explanation.definitionFit: To snare or ensnare something in a tangle, as a net does, is to catch it.

clue.text: Leg got broken in little bar

indicators.note: broken says the letters of leg got are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone broke a leg in a small pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little bar' suggests a pub, but it is a short wooden peg used as a fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A short rod pushed through a loop to fasten a duffel coat is a small bar.

clue.text: Central core of bandsmen, Blockheads, forming as a group

indicators.note: the central core of the two words says the letters sit inside them, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: The heart of a rock band's line-up, the Blockheads, playing together.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blockheads were Ian Dury's British rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase used in English for all together, as a single unit.

clue.text: No end of good fortune concerning money

indicators.note: no end of says the final letter of the word for good fortune is dropped

parts.note: luck is good fortune
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Endless good luck where cash is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'plenty of', but it removes the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy lucre is a disparaging term for cash, especially when gained dishonestly.

clue.text: Where you can't get in a word or aside?

definitions.text: Where you can't get in a word or aside?

parts.words: Where you can't get in a word or aside?
parts.note: recalls the idiom about failing to get a word in, with aside hinting at sideways

explanation.surface: Complaining of a chatterbox who never lets you speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is not getting a word in when someone talks nonstop; the word also means sideways, which 'aside' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Means sideways on, and completes the idiom about being unable to interject.

parts.note: a tickler is a puzzling or tricky problem

explanation.surface: A fussy person's second tricky question.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant who insists on exact rules is a fussy perfectionist.

clue.text: Learners in swimming-bath going backwards move along in ungainly style

indicators.note: in says the learners go inside the swimming-bath word
going backwards says the swimming-bath word is read in reverse

parts.note: a pool is a swimming bath
L is a learner, from the learner-driver plate, so two make LL

explanation.surface: Novices swimming backstroke clumsily along a pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The learners come from the L-plates that British learner drivers display; two of them are needed for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound or lumber along clumsily, like a big dog, is a synonym for galumph.

indicators.note: redraw says the letters of triangle are drawn again in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction that redrawing a triangle is vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Something integral is a necessary part of a whole, synonymous with fundamental.
